qt: to the Commission Sophie Wilmès (Renew), Gaetano Pedulla' (The Left), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Olivier Chastel (Renew), Hilde Vautmans (Renew), Ilhan Kyuchyuk (Renew), Oihane Agirregoitia Martínez (Renew), Wouter Beke (PPE), Villy Søvndal (Verts/ALE), JanChristoph Oetjen (Renew), Elisabetta Gualmini (Renew), Charles Goerens (Renew), Damian Boeselager (Verts/ALE), Nela Riehl (Verts/ALE), Daniel Freund (Verts/ALE), Lukas Sieper (Renew) Subject:

In its communication entitled ‘Preparing for a wider Union’1, the Commission proposes introducing temporary post-accession safeguards, potentially including the suspension of Council voting rights, as an additional mechanism alongside Article 7 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU). In parallel, it envisages engaging with Parliament and the Council to improve the effectiveness of Article 7 procedures within the existing Treaty framework. Therefore: 1.

How would the proposed accession safeguards, notably decisions under a reverse qualified-majority mechanism, interact with Article 7 TEU, and how would equal treatment under Article 4(2) TEU be ensured?
What format, deliverables and timetable does the Commission envisage for its engagement with Parliament and the Council regarding Article 7?

Given that four candidate countries are already assessed in both reporting exercises, how will the Commission avoid overlapping assessments and reporting burdens, ensure consistent findings and demonstrate the distinct added value of extending the rule of law report?
Commission communication of 10 October 2026 entitled ‘Preparing for a wider Union’ (COM(2026)0705),https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=celex:52026DC0705. 1
